स्थित, अस्, आ, अम्, stood, stayed, remained,
stopped; standing; standing up, risen; staying,
resting, abiding, (उच्चावचेषु स्थित, abiding in
all things high and low); being, situated, existing,
living; stood still, standing still, desisted, stopped;
fixed, permanent, settled, steady, firm, immovable;
steadfast, determined, resolved, decreed, established;
steady or steadfast in conduct; faithful to a promise
or agreement; upright, virtuous; agreed, engaged,
contracted, promised; being close at hand, ready;
(अम्), n. (in Vedic grammar), scil. पद, a word
standing by itself (i. e. without the particle इति in
the Pada text; opposed to उप-स्थित).
—स्थित-
धी, ईस्, ईस्, इ, steady-minded, firm-minded, firm,
unmoved, calm.
—स्थित-पाठ्य, (in the drama)
recitation in Prākṛt by a woman standing.
—स्थित-
प्रज्ञ, अस्, आ, अम्, firm in judgment or wisdom,
free from fancies or hallucinations, calm, contented.
—स्थित-प्रेमन्, आ, m. ‘firm in affection,’ a firm
or faithful friend.
—स्थितोपस्थित (˚त-उप्˚), अस्,
आ, अम्, (a word) with and without the particle इति
(in the Pada text; see स्थित above).
स्थित स्थित, स्थिति, &c. See p. 1147, col. 1.

स्थितवत्, आन्, अती, अत्, one who has stood or
stayed or abided.

स्थिति, इस्, f. standing, staying, remaining, con-
tinuing, living, residing, abiding; stay, residence;
standing still, stopping, continuance in one state;
remaining stationary, stability, duration, fixedness,
fixity, a firm position; stop, cessation; pause; any
[]
situation, state, position; posture, condition, natural
state, state of a case; good condition, well-doing,
welfare; station, high station, rank, dignity; per-
manence; continuance or steadfastness in the path
of duty, steadiness, correctness of conduct, propriety,
good manners; consistency; establishment of good
order (in a government); settled rule, sure or fixed
decision, ordinance, decree, axiom, maxim; settled
determination; term, limit, boundary; (in philo-
sophy) inertia, resistance to motion; one of the
three states through which the system of created
things and every individual being passes, (these
three states are, 1. उत्पत्ति, arising into being;
2. स्थिति, continuance in life; 3. लय, dissolution);
(in astronomy) duration of an eclipse; (in Vedic
grammar) the standing of a word by itself (i. e.
without the particle इति, see स्थित).
—स्थिति-मत्,
आन्, अती, अत्, possessing firmness or stability, firm,
stable; steady (in purpose or conduct), upright,
firm, virtuous.
—स्थिति-स्थापक, अस्, आ, अम्, fixing
in a (former or original) state or condition, capable
of placing in or restoring to a (previous) form or
position, having elastic properties; (अस्), m. (ac-
cording to some also अम्, n.), the capability of
placing in or recovering a (previous) position or
condition, elasticity.

स्थित्वा, ind. having stood or stayed or stopped,
&c.

स्थिर, अस्, आ, अम्, firm, fixed, steady, steadfast;
unfluctuating, permanent, enduring, durable, settled,
lasting; not moving, immovable, still, placid, calm,
quiescent, cool, composed, collected, free from pas-
sion; steadfast or steady in conduct; constant,
faithful, determined; certain, sure, convinced; firm,
hard, solid, strong; (अस्), m. a deity, immortal;
epithet of Śiva; of Kārttikeya; a mountain; a
tree; a bull; final emancipation from existence;
the planet Saturn; a particular plant (= 1. धव);
N. of a particular astronomical Yoga; of certain
zodiacal signs (viz. Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius;
so called because any work done under these signs
is supposed to be lasting); (आ), f. a strong-minded
woman; the earth; the shrub Śāla-parṇī; a medi-
cinal root (= काकोली); the silk-cotton tree; [cf. Gr.
στερεό-ς, στεῤῤό-ς, στέρι-φο-ς, στερίφη, στεῖρα,
στήρ-ιγξ, στηρίζ-ω, στελεόν: Lat. steri-li-s, stīr-
ia, stilla, stolidus, stultus: Goth. stairo: Old
Germ. staren, storren, stornen, ga-starken, starh-
jan, &c.: Angl. Sax. starian, starc: Lith. styr-u,
‘to be stiff or benumbed;’ ster-va, ‘a carcass.’]
—स्थिर-कुट्टक, अस्, m. (in algebra) a steady
pulverizer, constant multiplier, common divisor (ap-
plied to a particular kind of common divisor).
—स्थिर-गन्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, having durable per-
fume, strong-scented; (अस्), m. the Campaka tree,
Michelia Champaca; (आ), f. Pandanus Odoratissimus
(= केतकी); the trumpet-flower (= पाटला).
—स्थि-
र-चक्र, अस्, m. a particular Jina or Bodhi-sattva
(= मञ्जु-श्री).
—स्थिर-चित्त, अस्, आ, अम्, or स्थिर-
चेतस्, आस्, आस्, अस्, firm-minded, firm, resolute, constant,
steady.
—स्थिर-च्छद, अस्, m. ‘firm-leafed,’ the
birch tree (= भूर्ज-पत्त्र).
—स्थिर-च्छाय, अस्,
m. ‘having deep shade,’ a tree which gives shelter to
travellers; any tree.
—स्थिर-जिह्व, अस्, m. ‘firm-
tongued,’ a fish.
—स्थिर-जीविता, f. ‘firm-lived,’ the
silk-cotton tree.
—स्थिर-तर, अस्, आ, अम्, more
firm, fixed, stationary; very firm or permanent,
durable, eternal.
—स्थिर-ता, f. or स्थिर-त्व, अम्,
n. firmness, stability, steadiness, steadfastness; moral
firmness, fortitude; fearlessness.
—स्थिर-दंष्ट्र,
अस्, m. ‘strong-toothed,’ a snake; N. of Viṣṇu in
the boar-Avatāra; = ध्वनि (according to Śabda-k.).
—स्थिर-धन्वन्, आ, आ, अ, having or armed with
a strong bow (said of Rudra, Ṛg-veda

).
—स्थिर-धी, ईस्, ईस्, इ, firm-minded, resolute, per-
severing.
—स्थिर-पत्त्र, अस्, m. ‘firm-leafed,’ the
marshy date tree.
—स्थिर-पुष्प, अस्, m. ‘firm-
flowered,’ the Campaka tree; the Vakula tree.
—स्थिर-पुष्पिन्, ई, m. ‘strong-flowered,’ the
Tilaka tree.
—स्थिर-प्रतिज्ञ, अस्, आ, अम्, persist-
ing in an assertion, pertinacious; faithful to a promise.
[]
—स्थिर-प्रतिबन्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, firm in resist-
ance, pertinacious, obstinate.
—स्थिर-प्रतिष्ठा,
f. a firm resting-place, fixed residence.
—स्थिर-
प्रेमन्, आ, आ, अ, firm or steady in affection, a firm
friend.
—स्थिर-प्स्नु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. having con-
stant food; [cf. विश्व-प्स्न्य.]
—स्थिर-फला, f.
‘having firm fruit,’ a kind of gourd (= कुष्-
माण्डी).
—स्थिर-बुद्धि, इस्, इस्, इ, steady-minded,
resolute, calm, dispassionate.
—स्थिर-मति, इस्, f. a
firm mind, fixed resolution; (इस्, इस्, इ), firm-minded,
firm, steady, resolute.
—स्थिर-मनस्, आस्, आस्, अस्,
firm-minded, resolute, determined, faithful.
—स्थिर-
योनि, इस्, m. ‘having a firm receptacle,’ a large tree
which gives shade and shelter.
—स्थिर-यौवन,
अस्, आ, अम्, possessing constant youth, ever youthful;
(अस्), m. a kind of good or evil genius, a fairy (=
विद्या-धर).
—स्थिर-रङ्गा, f. ‘having a durable
colour,’ indigo; a sort of Curcuma.
—स्थिर-रागा,
f. a kind of Curcuma (= दारु-हरिद्रा).
—स्थिर-
लोचन, अस्, आ, अम्, steady-eyed; (one) whose gaze
is fixed.
—स्थिर-श्री, ईस्, ईस्, इ, having fixed or en-
during prosperity.
—स्थिर-सङ्गर, अस्, आ, अम्,
faithful to an agreement or promise, true, veracious.
—स्थिर-साधनक, अस्, m. the Sindu-vāra tree.
—स्थिर-सार, अस्, m. ‘having firm sap,’ a kind of
tree (= शाक).
—स्थिर-सौहृद, अस्, आ, अम्, firm
in friendship; (अम्), n. firmness in friendship.
—स्थिर-स्थायिन्, ई, इनी, इ, remaining firm or
steady, keeping perfectly still (as in meditation).
—स्थिरांह्रिप (˚र-अं˚), अस्, m. ‘durable tree,’
the marshy date tree.
—स्थिरात्मन् (˚र-आत्˚), आ, आ,
अ, firm-minded, resolute, unmoved, stable, steady.
—स्थिरानुराग (˚र-अन्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, constant in
affection or love.
—स्थिरायुस् (˚र-आय्˚), उस्, उस्, उस्,
long-lived, long-lasting; (उस्), m. the silk-cotton
tree, (also स्थिरायु according to some.)
—स्थिरा-
रम्भ (˚र-आर्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, firm in undertakings,
persevering.
—स्थिरी-कृ, cl. 8. P. -करोति, &c., to
make firm, confirm, strengthen, corroborate; to
bring to a standstill, stop, make fast.
—स्थिरी-भू,
cl. 1. P. -भवति, &c., to become firm or steady;
to become calm.
स्थिरक, अस्, m., N. of a preceptor.

स्थिराय, Nom. P. स्थिरायति, &c., to remain
firm or constant.

स्थिक स्थिक, अस्, m. (according to some
fr. rt. 1. स्था), the buttocks (= कटि-प्रोथ).

स्थिर् स्थिर्, cl. 1. P. स्थिरति, &c., (see
Nirukta

, (ac-
cording to Sāy. स्थिविभ्यः apparently = कुसीदे-
भ्यः, but the MS. is doubtful.)
